results.name: west-virginia
results.question: A state made during the war
results.popup:
West Virginia in 1863

Union slave state (border state)

Side: Union.

Became a state on June 20, 1863. In 1861 it was part of Virginia, which seceded. Slavery was still legal here; the new state's constitution freed enslaved people only gradually.

Tennessee in 1863

Seceded after Fort Sumter (April 1861)

Side: Confederacy. Seceded: June 8, 1861.

Voters approved secession on June 8, 1861. Union forces held much of the state from 1862.

results.name: sand-creek
results.question: A site that was not a battle
results.popup:
Sand Creek

The site of the Sand Creek Massacre, in Colorado. In November 1864 United States volunteer troops attacked a Cheyenne and Arapaho village here.

The area mapped is about 55,800 acres.

The National Park Service maps this area with its Civil War battlefields. It was an attack on a village, not a battle.

results.name: bear-river
results.question: A site that was not a battle
results.popup:
Bear River

The site of the Bear River Massacre, in Idaho. In January 1863 United States volunteer troops attacked a Northwestern Shoshone village here.

The area mapped is about 3,600 acres.

The National Park Service maps this area with its Civil War battlefields. It was an attack on a village, not a battle.
